396	    # -- pre-key claims ----------------------------------------------------
397	
398	    @staticmethod
399	    def claim_view(claim: PreKeyClaim) -> Dict[str, Any]:
400	        """Copy one claim into its public six-field view."""
401	        return {
402	            "claim_id": claim.claim_id,
403	            "recipient_device_id": claim.recipient_device_id,
404	            "identity_key": claim.identity_key,
405	            "key_id": claim.key_id,
406	            "public_key": claim.public_key,
407	            "claimed_at": claim.claimed_at,
408	        }
409	
410	    def claim_prekey(self, recipient_device_id: str, claim_id: str
411	                     ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
412	        """Atomically claim one of a device's one-time pre-keys.
413	
414	        The whole check-and-consume runs under the store lock — the same lock
415	        session creation and device/key revocations take — so concurrent
416	        claims, session creations and revocations are linearized and exactly
417	        one claim wins a race for the last available key.
418	
419	        A previously committed *claim_id* is idempotent: its frozen record is
420	        returned unchanged (``created`` False -> 200) and no further key is
421	        consumed, regardless of intervening rotation or revocation. A fresh
422	        *claim_id* takes the first pre-key (insertion order) that is neither
423	        revoked nor already consumed, marks it consumed, and records the
424	        claim. Unknown recipient -> :class:`PreKeyClaimError`
425	        ``recipient_unknown`` (404); revoked recipient -> ``recipient_revoked``
426	        (409); no available key -> ``prekey_unavailable`` (409/field
427	        ``prekey_id``). On failure nothing is written.
428	        """
429	        with self._lock:
430	            existing = self._prekey_claims.get(claim_id)
431	            if existing is not None:
432	                return self.claim_view(existing), False
433	            # claim_ids are a shared namespace: an id already committed by a
434	            # batch claim cannot also start a single-device claim.
435	            existing_batch = self._prekey_batch_claims.get(claim_id)
436	            if existing_batch is not None:
437	                raise PreKeyClaimError(CLAIM_ID_CONFLICT)
438	
439	            recipient_key = self._device_index.get(recipient_device_id)
440	            recipient = (self._devices.get(recipient_key)
441	                         if recipient_key is not None else None)
442	            if recipient is None:
443	                raise PreKeyClaimError(CLAIM_RECIPIENT_UNKNOWN)
444	            if recipient.revoked:
445	                raise PreKeyClaimError(CLAIM_RECIPIENT_REVOKED)
446	
447	            available = next((pk for pk in recipient.prekeys
448	                              if not pk.revoked and not pk.consumed), None)
449	            if available is None:
450	                raise PreKeyClaimError(CLAIM_NO_PREKEY)
451	
452	            available.consumed = True
453	            claim = PreKeyClaim(
454	                claim_id=claim_id,
455	                recipient_device_id=recipient_device_id,
456	                key_id=available.key_id,
457	                identity_key=recipient.identity_key,
458	                public_key=available.public_key,
459	            )
460	            self._prekey_claims[claim_id] = claim
461	            self._notify_change()
462	            return self.claim_view(claim), True
463	
464	    # -- user-wide batch pre-key claims -----------------------------------
465	
466	    @staticmethod
467	    def batch_claim_view(claim: PreKeyBatchClaim) -> Dict[str, Any]:
468	        """Copy one batch claim into its public response view."""
469	        return {
470	            "claim_id": claim.claim_id,
471	            "user_id": claim.user_id,
472	            "claimed_at": claim.claimed_at,
473	            "devices": [{
474	                "device_id": entry.device_id,
475	                "identity_key": entry.identity_key,
476	                "key_id": entry.key_id,
477	                "public_key": entry.public_key,
478	            } for entry in claim.devices],
479	        }
480	
481	    def claim_prekey_batch(self, user_id: str, claim_id: str
482	                           ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
483	        """Atomically claim one pre-key on every active device of a user.
484	
485	        The user's devices are enumerated in registration order, skipping
486	        revoked devices. For each active device the first pre-key
487	        (insertion order) that is neither revoked nor consumed is selected.
488	        Selection runs first for *every* device; only when all devices have
489	        an available key are all of them marked consumed at once and the
490	        batch record written, so a device short of a key aborts the whole
491	        claim and no key on any device is consumed. The whole check-and-
492	        consume holds the store lock — the same lock single claims, session
493	        creation, revocations and pre-key replenishment take — so all of
494	        those linearize together.
495	
496	        A previously committed batch *claim_id* is idempotent: its frozen
497	        record is returned unchanged (``created`` False -> 200) and no
498	        further key is consumed, regardless of later rotation/revocation.
499	        A user with no registered device raises
500	        :class:`PreKeyBatchClaimError` ``user_unknown`` (404/field
501	        ``user_id``); one whose devices are all revoked raises
502	        ``no_active_device`` (409/field ``device_id``); any active device
503	        without an available key raises ``prekey_unavailable`` (409/field
504	        ``prekey_id``). On failure nothing is written.
505	        """
506	        with self._lock:
507	            existing = self._prekey_batch_claims.get(claim_id)
508	            if existing is not None:
509	                return self.batch_claim_view(existing), False
510	            # claim_ids are one shared namespace with single claims: an id
511	            # already committed by a single claim cannot start a batch claim
512	            # (the persisted sections would otherwise collide on restart).
513	            if claim_id in self._prekey_claims:
514	                raise PreKeyBatchClaimError(CLAIM_ID_CONFLICT)
515	
516	            user_devices = [device for key, device in self._devices.items()
517	                            if key[0] == user_id]
518	            if not user_devices:
519	                raise PreKeyBatchClaimError(BATCH_CLAIM_USER_UNKNOWN)
520	            active_devices = [device for device in user_devices
521	                              if not device.revoked]
522	            if not active_devices:
523	                raise PreKeyBatchClaimError(BATCH_CLAIM_NO_ACTIVE_DEVICE)
524	
525	            # Select first, consume after: build the full (device, key) list
526	            # before mutating anything, so one device without a key aborts
527	            # the entire batch with zero consumption.
528	            selections: List[Tuple[Device, SignedPreKey]] = []
529	            for device in active_devices:
530	                available = next((pk for pk in device.prekeys
531	                                  if not pk.revoked and not pk.consumed), None)
532	                if available is None:
533	                    raise PreKeyBatchClaimError(BATCH_CLAIM_NO_PREKEY)
534	                selections.append((device, available))
535	
536	            entries: List[BatchClaimDevice] = []
537	            for device, prekey in selections:
538	                prekey.consumed = True
539	                entries.append(BatchClaimDevice(
540	                    device_id=device.device_id,
541	                    identity_key=device.identity_key,
542	                    key_id=prekey.key_id,
543	                    public_key=prekey.public_key))
544	            batch = PreKeyBatchClaim(
545	                claim_id=claim_id, user_id=user_id, devices=entries)
546	            self._prekey_batch_claims[claim_id] = batch
547	            self._notify_change()
548	            return self.batch_claim_view(batch), True

551	
552	    def create_session(self, initiator_device_id: str, recipient_device_id: str,
553	                       prekey_id: str, ephemeral_key: str) -> Session:
554	        """Atomically validate and create one session.
555	
556	        Lookups, revocation checks and the insert all happen while holding the
557	        store lock (the same lock device/pre-key revocations take), so a
558	        concurrent revocation is linearized either wholly before this call
559	        (then it fails) or wholly after it (then the session is retained).
560	        On any failure nothing is written and :class:`SessionCreateError`
561	        carries the reason.
562	        """
563	        with self._lock:
564	            initiator = self._device_index.get(initiator_device_id)
565	            initiator = self._devices.get(initiator) if initiator is not None else None
566	            if initiator is None:
567	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_INITIATOR_UNKNOWN)
568	            if initiator.revoked:
569	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_INITIATOR_REVOKED)
570	
571	            recipient_key = self._device_index.get(recipient_device_id)
572	            recipient = (self._devices.get(recipient_key)
573	                         if recipient_key is not None else None)
574	            if recipient is None:
575	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_RECIPIENT_UNKNOWN)
576	            if recipient.revoked:
577	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_RECIPIENT_REVOKED)
578	
579	            used_prekey = next((pk for pk in recipient.prekeys
580	                                if pk.key_id == prekey_id), None)
581	            if used_prekey is None:
582	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_PREKEY_UNKNOWN)
583	            if used_prekey.revoked:
584	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_PREKEY_REVOKED)
585	            if used_prekey.consumed:
586	                raise SessionCreateError(SESSION_PREKEY_CONSUMED)
587	
588	            session = Session(
589	                session_id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
590	                initiator_device_id=initiator_device_id,
591	                recipient_device_id=recipient_device_id,
592	                prekey_id=prekey_id,
593	                ephemeral_key=ephemeral_key,
594	                identity_key=recipient.identity_key,
595	                public_key=used_prekey.public_key,
596	            )
597	            self._sessions[session.session_id] = session
598	            self._notify_change()
599	            return session
600	
601	    def create_session_from_claim(self, claim_id: str,
602	                                  initiator_device_id: str,
603	                                  ephemeral_key: str) -> Session:
604	        """Atomically establish one session from a committed pre-key claim.
605	
606	        The whole check-and-write runs under the store lock — the same lock
607	        taken by claims, ordinary session creation and device/pre-key
608	        revocations — so the binding check, every status check and the two
609	        inserts (session plus the claim binding) linearize together and each
610	        ``claim_id`` can win at most once, however many requests race.
611	
612	        A ``claim_id`` without a committed claim is a 404; one whose binding
613	        already exists is a 409 (``claim_id``), and the repeat creates no
614	        session. An unknown initiator is a 404 and a revoked initiator a 409
615	        (``initiator_device_id``); revocation after the claim of the claim's
616	        recipient device or pre-key is a 409 naming ``recipient_device_id`` or
617	        ``prekey_id`` respectively. On success the session freezes the claim's
618	        ``recipient_device_id``, ``prekey_id``, ``identity_key`` and
619	        ``public_key`` at claim time; the initiator and ephemeral key come
620	        from the request. On any failure nothing is written.
621	        """
622	        with self._lock:
623	            if claim_id in self._claim_session_bindings:
624	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_DUPLICATE)
625	
626	            claim = self._prekey_claims.get(claim_id)
627	            if claim is None:
628	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_CLAIM_UNKNOWN)
629	
630	            initiator_key = self._device_index.get(initiator_device_id)
631	            initiator = (self._devices.get(initiator_key)
632	                         if initiator_key is not None else None)
633	            if initiator is None:
634	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_INITIATOR_UNKNOWN)
635	            if initiator.revoked:
636	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_INITIATOR_REVOKED)
637	
638	            recipient_key = self._device_index.get(claim.recipient_device_id)
639	            recipient = (self._devices.get(recipient_key)
640	                         if recipient_key is not None else None)
641	            if recipient is None:
642	                # A committed claim always names a registered device
643	                # (restore_state enforces it and devices are never deleted);
644	                # reaching here means no usable recipient remains.
645	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_RECIPIENT_REVOKED)
646	            if recipient.revoked:
647	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_RECIPIENT_REVOKED)
648	
649	            used_prekey = next((pk for pk in recipient.prekeys
650	                                if pk.key_id == claim.key_id), None)
651	            if used_prekey is None or used_prekey.revoked:
652	                raise ClaimSessionError(CLAIM_SESSION_PREKEY_REVOKED)
653	
654	            session = Session(
655	                session_id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
656	                initiator_device_id=initiator_device_id,
657	                recipient_device_id=claim.recipient_device_id,
658	                prekey_id=claim.key_id,
659	                ephemeral_key=ephemeral_key,
660	                identity_key=claim.identity_key,
661	                public_key=claim.public_key,
662	            )
663	            self._sessions[session.session_id] = session
664	            self._claim_session_bindings[claim_id] = ClaimSessionBinding(
665	                claim_id=claim_id,
666	                session_id=session.session_id,
667	                recipient_device_id=claim.recipient_device_id,
668	                prekey_id=claim.key_id,
669	                identity_key=claim.identity_key,
670	                public_key=claim.public_key,
671	                created_at=session.created_at)
672	            self._notify_change()
673	            return session
674	
675	    def session_view(self, session_id: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
676	        """Return the immutable eight-field snapshot of a session, or ``None``.
677	
678	        The values are copied under the lock; session records are never
679	        mutated after creation, so revocations cannot change this view.
680	        """
681	        with self._lock:
682	            session = self._sessions.get(session_id)
683	            if session is None:
684	                return None
685	            return {
686	                "session_id": session.session_id,
687	                "initiator_device_id": session.initiator_device_id,
688	                "recipient_device_id": session.recipient_device_id,
689	                "prekey_id": session.prekey_id,
690	                "ephemeral_key": session.ephemeral_key,
691	                "identity_key": session.identity_key,
692	                "public_key": session.public_key,
693	                "created_at": session.created_at,

698	    @staticmethod
699	    def group_view(group: Group) -> Dict[str, Any]:
700	        """Copy one group into its public five-field view."""
701	        return {
702	            "group_id": group.group_id,
703	            "revision": group.revision,
704	            "members": list(group.members),
705	            "created_at": group.created_at,
706	        }

708	    def create_group(self, group_id: str, creator_device_id: str,
709	                     member_device_ids: List[str]) -> Group:
710	        """Atomically validate and create one group.
711	
712	        The id must be unused and the creator an active registered device.
713	        Member ids are arbitrary non-empty strings already validated by the
714	        service; they need not resolve to registered devices and are stored
715	        as given. The creator is always the first member; the other ids
716	        follow in request order, de-duplicated (a repeated id kept once).
717	        The creator check and the insert happen under the store lock, the
718	        same lock device revocations take, so a concurrent revocation is
719	        linearized either wholly before this call (then it fails) or wholly
720	        after it (then the group is retained). On failure nothing is written.
721	        """
722	        with self._lock:
723	            if group_id in self._groups:
724	                raise GroupError(GROUP_DUPLICATE_ID)
725	
726	            creator = self._active_device(creator_device_id)
727	            if creator is None:
728	                existing = self._find_device(creator_device_id)
729	                raise GroupError(GROUP_CREATOR_REVOKED if existing is not None
730	                                 else GROUP_CREATOR_UNKNOWN)
731	
732	            members: List[str] = [creator_device_id]
733	            seen = {creator_device_id}
734	            for device_id in member_device_ids:
735	                if device_id not in seen:
736	                    seen.add(device_id)
737	                    members.append(device_id)
738	
739	            group = Group(group_id=group_id,
740	                          creator_device_id=creator_device_id, members=members)
741	            self._groups[group_id] = group
742	            self._notify_change()
743	            return group
744	
745	    def get_group(self, group_id: str) -> Optional[Group]:
746	        """Return the stored group, or ``None`` when the id is unknown."""
747	        with self._lock:
748	            return self._groups.get(group_id)
749	
750	    def _find_device(self, device_id: str) -> Optional[Device]:
751	        """Resolve a globally-addressed device (must hold the lock)."""
752	        key = self._device_index.get(device_id)
753	        return self._devices.get(key) if key is not None else None
754	
755	    def _active_device(self, device_id: str) -> Optional[Device]:
756	        """Resolve a device that exists and is not revoked (must hold lock)."""
757	        device = self._find_device(device_id)
758	        if device is None or device.revoked:
759	            return None
760	        return device

762	    def _authorize_group_actor(self, group_id: str,
763	                               actor_device_id: str) -> Group:
764	        """Resolve a group and authorize its creator (must hold the lock).
765	
766	        Unknown group -> ``group_unknown``; an unknown or revoked actor ->
767	        ``actor_unknown`` / ``actor_revoked``; an active non-creator ->
768	        ``actor_not_creator``.
769	        """
770	        group = self._groups.get(group_id)
771	        if group is None:
772	            raise GroupError(GROUP_UNKNOWN)
773	        actor = self._find_device(actor_device_id)
774	        if actor is None:
775	            raise GroupError(GROUP_ACTOR_UNKNOWN)
776	        if actor.revoked:
777	            raise GroupError(GROUP_ACTOR_REVOKED)
778	        if actor_device_id != group.creator_device_id:
779	            raise GroupError(GROUP_ACTOR_NOT_CREATOR)
780	        return group

782	    def add_group_member(self, group_id: str, actor_device_id: str,
783	                         device_id: str) -> Tuple[Group, bool]:
784	        """Atomically authorize the creator and add one member.
785	
786	        Returns ``(group, created)``: ``created`` is False (200) when the
787	        active device is already a member, True (201) when it was appended.
788	        An unknown or revoked target device raises ``group_device_unknown``
789	        / ``group_device_revoked`` (404 / 409, field ``device_id``). A
790	        successful append advances the group revision; an idempotent repeat
791	        does not.
792	        """
793	        with self._lock:
794	            group = self._authorize_group_actor(group_id, actor_device_id)
795	            if device_id in group.members:
796	                return group, False
797	            target = self._find_device(device_id)
798	            if target is None:
799	                raise GroupError(GROUP_DEVICE_UNKNOWN)
800	            if target.revoked:
801	                raise GroupError(GROUP_DEVICE_REVOKED)
802	            group.members.append(device_id)
803	            group.revision += 1
804	            self._notify_change()
805	            return group, True
806	
807	    def remove_group_member(self, group_id: str, actor_device_id: str,
808	                            device_id: str) -> Group:
809	        """Atomically authorize the creator and remove one member.
810	
811	        Always succeeds with 200 semantics: a target id that is not (or no
812	        longer) on the member list is an idempotent no-op leaving the
813	        revision untouched, and a revoked device may still be removed so no
814	        revoked id lingers on the roster. The one hard failure besides the
815	        shared authorization checks is an id that has never been a
816	        registered device (``group_device_unknown`` -> 404). The creator
817	        cannot leave their own group; that request is a no-op that keeps
818	        the creator as the first member.
819	        """
820	        with self._lock:
821	            group = self._authorize_group_actor(group_id, actor_device_id)
822	            if device_id == group.creator_device_id:
823	                return group
824	            if self._find_device(device_id) is None:
825	                raise GroupError(GROUP_DEVICE_UNKNOWN)
826	            if device_id in group.members:
827	                group.members.remove(device_id)
828	                group.revision += 1
829	                self._notify_change()
830	            return group

844	    def create_group_session(self, group_id: str, initiator_device_id: str,
845	                             ephemeral_key: str) -> GroupSession:

848	        Every request creates a fresh session (a new ``session_id``);
849	        repeated POSTs are never deduplicated. The member list and group
850	        revision are frozen at creation, so later membership changes cannot
851	        alter the snapshot. The initiator must be an active *current* member
852	        of the group. On failure nothing is written.

867	                session_id=uuid.uuid4().hex,
868	                group_id=group_id,
869	                initiator_device_id=initiator_device_id,
870	                ephemeral_key=ephemeral_key,
871	                members=list(group.members),
872	                revision=group.revision,

909	    def _authorize_sync_device(self, session_id: str, device_id: str
910	                               ) -> GroupSession:
911	        """Resolve a group session and authorize a frozen-member device.
912	
913	        Must be called while holding the store lock. Distinguishes an unknown
914	        session (``session_unknown``) from device-side failures
915	        (``device_unknown`` / ``device_inactive`` / ``device_not_member``);
916	        the service maps all three device failures to 409/device_id.
917	        Membership is the frozen snapshot, so a removed member still syncs
918	        and a later-added member cannot.
919	        """
920	        session = self._group_sessions.get(session_id)
921	        if session is None:
922	            raise GroupSyncError(SYNC_SESSION_UNKNOWN)
923	        device = self._find_device(device_id)
924	        if device is None:
925	            raise GroupSyncError(SYNC_DEVICE_UNKNOWN)
926	        if device.revoked:
927	            raise GroupSyncError(SYNC_DEVICE_INACTIVE)
928	        if device_id not in session.members:
929	            raise GroupSyncError(SYNC_DEVICE_NOT_MEMBER)
930	        return session

932	    def group_sync_page(self, session_id: str, device_id: str,
933	                        after: Optional[int], limit: int) -> Dict[str, Any]:
934	        """Atomically read one ascending sync page, advancing the device cursor.
935	
936	        When *after* is ``None`` the device's stored cursor is the starting
937	        point and the cursor advances to the page's last sequence (an empty
938	        page leaves it unchanged). An explicit *after* is a one-off query:
939	        the stored cursor is neither read nor moved.
940	        """
941	        with self._lock:
942	            self._authorize_sync_device(session_id, device_id)
943	            cursor_key = (session_id, device_id)
944	            record = self._group_sync_cursors.get(cursor_key)
945	            if after is None:
946	                start = record.cursor if record is not None else 0
947	                advance = True
948	            else:
949	                start = after
950	                advance = False
951	            stream = self._messages.get(session_id, [])
952	            page = [m for m in stream if m.sequence > start][:limit]

970	    def group_sync_checkpoint(self, session_id: str, device_id: str,
971	                              cursor: int
972	                              ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
973	        """Atomically move a device's sync cursor forward, or confirm equality.
974	
975	        *cursor* must not exceed the session's largest stored sequence. A
976	        strictly greater cursor creates/advances the record (201, refreshed
977	        ``updated_at``); an equal cursor is an idempotent no-op (200, the
978	        timestamp is untouched); a smaller cursor conflicts (409/
979	        ``cursor``). The authorization checks run first: an unknown session
980	        raises ``session_unknown`` and an unknown/revoked/non-member device
981	        raises the matching device reason (all mapped to 409/device_id by the
982	        service). Returns ``(view, advanced)``.
983	        """
984	        with self._lock:
985	            session = self._authorize_sync_device(session_id, device_id)
986	            stream = self._messages.get(session_id, [])
987	            max_sequence = stream[-1].sequence if stream else 0
988	            if cursor > max_sequence:
989	                raise GroupSyncError(SYNC_CURSOR_CONFLICT)
990	            cursor_key = (session_id, device_id)
991	            record = self._group_sync_cursors.get(cursor_key)
992	            current = record.cursor if record is not None else 0
993	            if cursor < current:
994	                raise GroupSyncError(SYNC_CURSOR_CONFLICT)
995	            advanced = cursor > current
996	            if advanced:
997	                if record is None:
998	                    record = GroupSyncCursor(cursor=cursor)
999	                    self._group_sync_cursors[cursor_key] = record
1000	                else:
1001	                    record.cursor = cursor
1002	                    record.updated_at = utc_now_iso()
1003	                self._notify_change()
1004	            if record is None:
1005	                # No cursor has ever been advanced: the checkpoint at 0 is an
1006	                # idempotent no-op anchored at the session's creation time.
1007	                record = GroupSyncCursor(cursor=0,
1008	                                         updated_at=session.created_at)
1009	            return self._checkpoint_view(session_id, device_id, record), advanced

1026	    def append_message(self, session_id: str, sender_device_id: str,
1027	                       message_id: str, sequence: int, nonce: str,
1028	                       ciphertext: str) -> Message:
1029	        """Atomically validate and append one message to a session's stream.
1030	
1031	        The session lookup, sender revocation check, duplicate-id check,
1032	        sequence-continuity check and session-scoped nonce-replay check all
1033	        happen while holding the store lock (the same lock device revocations
1034	        take), so a concurrent revocation is linearized either wholly before
1035	        this call (then it fails) or wholly after it (then the message is
1036	        retained). The checks have one fixed priority: unknown session,
1037	        inactive sender, duplicate message_id, bad sequence, duplicate nonce.
1038	        A nonce already accepted in this same session is a replay and fails
1039	        even when every other field is fresh; the identical nonce in a
1040	        different session is accepted. On any failure nothing is written and
1041	        :class:`MessageCreateError` carries the reason.
1042	        """
1043	        with self._lock:
1044	            group_session = self._group_sessions.get(session_id)
1045	            if session_id not in self._sessions and group_session is None:
1046	                raise MessageCreateError(MESSAGE_SESSION_UNKNOWN)
1047	
1048	            sender_key = self._device_index.get(sender_device_id)
1049	            sender = (self._devices.get(sender_key)
1050	                      if sender_key is not None else None)
1051	            if sender is None or sender.revoked:
1052	                raise MessageCreateError(MESSAGE_SENDER_INACTIVE)
1053	            # Only devices frozen into a group session may post into it; a
1054	            # device removed after the freeze is rejected like an inactive one.
1055	            if (group_session is not None
1056	                    and sender_device_id not in group_session.members):
1057	                raise MessageCreateError(MESSAGE_SENDER_INACTIVE)
1058	
1059	            stream = self._messages.setdefault(session_id, [])
1060	            if any(m.message_id == message_id for m in stream):
1061	                raise MessageCreateError(MESSAGE_DUPLICATE_ID)
1062	            expected = stream[-1].sequence + 1 if stream else 1
1063	            if sequence != expected:
1064	                raise MessageCreateError(MESSAGE_BAD_SEQUENCE)
1065	            used_nonces = self._used_nonces.setdefault(session_id, set())
1066	            # Nonces are compared exactly as received (raw string equality);
1067	            # a replay neither appends a message nor advances any sequence.
1068	            if nonce in used_nonces:
1069	                raise MessageCreateError(MESSAGE_DUPLICATE_NONCE)
1070	
1071	            message = Message(
1072	                session_id=session_id,
1073	                sender_device_id=sender_device_id,
1074	                message_id=message_id,
1075	                sequence=sequence,
1076	                nonce=nonce,
1077	                ciphertext=ciphertext,
1078	            )
1079	            stream.append(message)
1080	            used_nonces.add(nonce)
1081	            self._notify_change()
1082	            return message

1084	    def message_page(self, session_id: str, device_id: str, after: int,
1085	                     limit: int) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, Any]], int]:
1086	        """Atomically read one ascending page of a session's messages.
1087	
1088	        Returns ``(message_views, next_after)``: the envelopes with
1089	        ``sequence > after`` (ascending, at most *limit*) and the sequence to
1090	        resume from — the last returned sequence, or *after* itself when the
1091	        page is empty. The session lookup and the reader's revocation check
1092	        run under the store lock, so a concurrent revocation is linearized
1093	        either wholly before (then it fails) or wholly after this call.
1094	        """
1095	        with self._lock:
1096	            group_session = self._group_sessions.get(session_id)
1097	            if session_id not in self._sessions and group_session is None:
1098	                raise MessageListError(MESSAGE_SESSION_UNKNOWN)
1099	
1100	            device_key = self._device_index.get(device_id)
1101	            device = (self._devices.get(device_key)
1102	                      if device_key is not None else None)
1103	            if device is None or device.revoked:
1104	                raise MessageListError(MESSAGE_DEVICE_INACTIVE)
1105	            # Group sessions are readable by the frozen member set only; a
1106	            # device added or removed after the freeze is not a reader.
1107	            if group_session is not None and device_id not in \
1108	                    group_session.members:
1109	                raise MessageListError(MESSAGE_DEVICE_INACTIVE)
1110	
1111	            stream = self._messages.get(session_id, [])
1112	            page = [m for m in stream if m.sequence > after][:limit]
1113	            next_after = page[-1].sequence if page else after
1114	            return [self.message_view(m) for m in page], next_after

1118	    @staticmethod
1119	    def _delivery_view(session_id: str, message: Message,
1120	                       state: Optional["MessageDelivery"]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
1121	        """Build the five-field delivery status view of one message."""
1122	        return {
1123	            "session_id": session_id,
1124	            "message_id": message.message_id,
1125	            "status": "acked" if state is not None and state.acked
1126	            else "pending",

1131	    def _delivery_target(self, session_id: str, message_id: str,
1132	                         device_id: str
1133	                         ) -> Tuple[Session, Message]:
1134	        """Resolve and authorize a (session, message, recipient) triple.
1135	
1136	        Must be called while holding the store lock. Raises
1137	        :class:`DeliveryError` with the mapped reason on any failure.
1138	        """
1139	        session = self._sessions.get(session_id)
1140	        if session is None:
1141	            raise DeliveryError(DELIVERY_SESSION_UNKNOWN)
1142	        message = next((m for m in self._messages.get(session_id, [])
1143	                        if m.message_id == message_id), None)
1144	        if message is None:
1145	            raise DeliveryError(DELIVERY_MESSAGE_UNKNOWN)
1146	        device_key = self._device_index.get(device_id)
1147	        device = (self._devices.get(device_key)
1148	                  if device_key is not None else None)
1149	        if device is None or device.revoked:
1150	            raise DeliveryError(DELIVERY_DEVICE_INACTIVE)
1151	        if device_id != session.recipient_device_id:
1152	            raise DeliveryError(DELIVERY_DEVICE_MISMATCH)
1153	        return session, message

1155	    def retry_message(self, session_id: str, message_id: str,
1156	                      device_id: str, attempt_id: str
1157	                      ) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
1158	        """Atomically record one delivery attempt for a message.
1159	
1160	        The recipient must be the session's active recipient. Each distinct
1161	        ``attempt_id`` is counted exactly once, so retries with the same id
1162	        are idempotent. Returns ``(view, created)`` where ``created`` says
1163	        whether this is the first ever attempt for the message (201 vs 200).
1164	        Nothing changes on a failed authorization check.
1165	        """
1166	        with self._lock:
1167	            _, message = self._delivery_target(
1168	                session_id, message_id, device_id)
1169	            key = (session_id, message_id)
1170	            state = self._delivery.get(key)
1171	            created = state is None
1172	            if created:
1173	                state = MessageDelivery()
1174	                self._delivery[key] = state
1175	            if attempt_id not in state.attempt_ids:
1176	                state.attempt_ids.add(attempt_id)
1177	                state.attempts += 1
1178	            view = self._delivery_view(session_id, message, state)
1179	            self._notify_change()
1180	            return view, created

1182	    def ack_message(self, session_id: str, message_id: str, device_id: str,
1183	                    sequence: int) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], bool]:
1184	        """Atomically acknowledge a message for the active recipient.
1185	
1186	        ``sequence`` must equal the message's stored sequence. The first ack
1187	        marks the message acked; repeated acks are idempotent. Returns
1188	        ``(view, first_ack)``.
1189	        """
1190	        with self._lock:
1191	            _, message = self._delivery_target(
1192	                session_id, message_id, device_id)
1193	            if sequence != message.sequence:
1194	                raise DeliveryError(DELIVERY_BAD_SEQUENCE)
1195	            key = (session_id, message_id)
1196	            state = self._delivery.get(key)
1197	            first_ack = state is None or not state.acked
1198	            if state is None:
1199	                state = MessageDelivery()
1200	                self._delivery[key] = state
1201	            state.acked = True
1202	            state.ack_sequence = sequence
1203	            view = self._delivery_view(session_id, message, state)
1204	            self._notify_change()
1205	            return view, first_ack

1213	            state = self._delivery.get((session_id, message_id))
1214	            return self._delivery_view(session_id, message, state)
